title: State Acquisition and Tenancy Act
subtitle: East Bengal's landmark land law abolished intermediary interests and transformed rural property relations.
summary: The East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of 1950 created the legal basis for abolishing zamindari and intermediary rent-receiving interests, bringing land-revenue relations more directly under the state.
heroTagline: A post-Partition land law changed the structure of rural authority.
whyItMatters: The act marked one of the most consequential socio-economic reforms in East Bengal, linking Pakistan-period state formation to long-running peasant and land-rights demands.
longTermLegacy: The law remained central to Bangladesh's later land administration because it dismantled major colonial-era intermediaries while leaving new questions of land control and rural inequality.
identityMemoryNotes: It is remembered as a structural break from zamindari, though not as a complete solution to rural inequality.

claimCitations.claim: The East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act of 1950 created the legal basis for abolishing zamindari and intermediary rent-receiving interests, bringing land-revenue relations more directly under the state.
The act marked one of the most consequential socio-economic reforms in East Bengal, linking Pakistan-period state formation to long-running peasant and land-rights demands.
The law remained central to Bangladesh's later land administration because it dismantled major colonial-era intermediaries while leaving new questions of land control and rural inequality.
It is remembered as a structural break from zamindari, though not as a complete solution to rural inequality.
